content.user_title: Design Spring REST APIs for Allra
content.value_statement: Backend teams often lose consistency when adding Spring APIs and DTOs. This skill applies Allra conventions for package layout, REST naming, DTO records, validation, and responses.
actual_capabilities: Defines domain-based package structure for Allra Spring backend services.
Applies Request, Response, and internal DTO naming conventions.
Recommends Java record usage for simple DTO classes.
Guides REST endpoint naming for create, read, update, patch, and delete flows.
Shows Bean Validation expectations for request DTO fields.
Provides standard response and error response shape guidance.
limitations: Does not generate a complete working service without project context.
Does not replace security, authorization, or transaction design review.
Assumes Java 17 and Spring Boot 3.2 conventions unless the project differs.
Uses Allra-specific naming preferences that may not fit other organizations.

use_cases.title: Create a new domain API
use_cases.description: Generate a consistent package plan, DTO names, controller routes, and validation checklist for a new backend domain.

use_cases.title: Review API consistency
use_cases.description: Compare existing controller and DTO designs against Allra conventions before a pull request is merged.

use_cases.title: Guide AI-assisted backend work
use_cases.description: Keep Claude, Codex, or Claude Code aligned with Allra backend standards during implementation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a DTO Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for naming and validation guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the request and response DTOs for a new user signup API using Allra conventions. Include field validation recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a REST Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Allra-style Spring REST endpoint for creating products. Include route naming, package placement, DTO names, and response guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Package Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate cleanup of an existing backend module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend module structure and suggest changes that align it with Allra domain package rules and layer responsibilities.

prompt_templates.title: Audit API Design Before Merge
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Spring API design against Allra standards. Check package layout, REST naming, DTO suffixes, record usage, validation, and response consistency.

output_examples.input: Create a product creation API for an Allra backend service.
output: The result names the product domain package and separates API, DTO, entity, repository, and service layers.
It proposes CreateProductRequest and ProductResponse as the public DTO names.
It recommends required validation for product name and price fields.

output_examples.input: Review my user API structure for Allra standards.
output: The review flags package names that do not separate controller, DTO, repository, and service responsibilities.
It identifies DTOs that should use Request, Response, or Dto suffixes.
It checks whether request DTOs include validation rules.

output_examples.input: Plan internal DTOs for product query results and events.
output: The plan distinguishes client-facing DTOs from internal transfer objects.
It recommends Dto suffixes for internal query and event objects.
It notes where QueryDSL projection DTOs may be appropriate.

best_practices: Provide the target domain, endpoint purpose, and existing package names before asking for a design.
Ask for validation rules whenever a request DTO accepts client input.
Review generated designs against project-specific API versioning and response policies.
anti_patterns: Do not mix controller, service, repository, and entity classes in one package.
Do not use the Dto suffix for public request or response objects.
Do not copy sample response shapes without checking the project standard.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design Spring REST APIs, DTO names, validation rules, response shapes, and domain package structure for Allra backends.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides design guidance and examples. Production code still needs project context, tests, authorization, and persistence details.

faq.question: Which Java style does it prefer for DTOs?
faq.answer: It prefers Java records for simple request, response, and internal transfer objects when the project supports them.

faq.question: Can it be used outside Allra projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but the conventions are Allra-specific. Other teams should adapt names, routes, and response formats to their own standards.

faq.question: Does it cover API security?
faq.answer: Only basic validation guidance is included. Authentication, authorization, rate limits, and sensitive data handling need separate review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
